_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies". A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn. "cue" is when the talk comes on: "start" as the lesson opens, {"after": "<figure>"} once that figure's task is done, or "check" as the final check opens. "locals" names who in town asked a forecast question, by the forecast's "id" in the lesson file.

turns.them: CQ, CQ, CQ. This is W7DQ, Walla Walla, calling the new station at Harrow. Anybody up there, or did the wind carry you off to Idaho? Come back.

replies.say: W7DQ, this is W7HAR, Harrow. I’m here. I think.
replies.back: Fine signal. You sound about twelve years old, but that may be the static.
It’s on, and so is half of Adams County. A party line has nothing on a ham set. Give your call sign, tenderfoot.
Suspicious. I like that in a weather forecaster. W7DQ, Walla Walla. I’ve been reading skies down here since before you were born.

turns.them: Here’s the situation, as the Bureau explained it to me in a letter with too many carbon copies. Harrow has a wheat co-op, an airfield with one mail plane, and as of this week, you. Folks will knock on your door wanting to know what the sky is up to. Your job is to tell them, and to be right more often than Aunt Fern’s knee.

replies.back: My aunt. Her left knee has forecast rain every day since 1904. It’s been right about a third of the time, which is better than some fellows with diplomas.
Then a farmer loses a field of hay and you eat supper alone for a month. Small towns have long memories.
So does milking a cow, until you meet the cow.

turns.them: So here’s the arrangement. Every Tuesday evening we keep a sked, that’s a schedule, on this frequency. You study the lesson I send up on the train, you bring me the questions from town you can’t answer yet, and I’ll talk you through them. By harvest you’ll know every cloud in the sky.

replies.back: Like school, only the bell is a thunderstorm.
Good. Bring coffee. Mine has been on the stove since Coolidge.

turns.them: One more thing. I talk a fair amount. If you’d rather study in peace, say so, and I’ll keep my opinions to myself. Mostly.

replies.say: Keep the radio on. I’ll want the help.
replies.back: Splendid. Tuesday, then. Seventy-three: that’s ham for best regards.
Suit yourself. Books are good company and they don’t snore. If you change your mind, the dial is in Settings.
